import yfinance as yf
import pandas as pd

# Download stock data for TSLA, NVDA, GOOG and AAPL
tsla_data = yf.download('TSLA', start='2024-04-01', end='2024-06-20')
nvda_data = yf.download('NVDA', start='2024-04-01', end='2024-06-20')
goog_data = yf.download('GOOG', start='2024-04-01', end='2024-06-20')
aapl_data = yf.download('AAPL', start='2024-04-01', end='2024-06-20')
# Extract 'Close' prices and rename columns
tsla_close = tsla_data['Close'].rename('TSLA')
nvda_close = nvda_data['Close'].rename('NVDA')
goog_close = goog_data['Close'].rename('GOOG')
aapl_close = aapl_data['Close'].rename('AAPL')
# Extract 'Volume' and rename columns
tsla_volume = tsla_data['Volume'].rename('TSLA')
nvda_volume = nvda_data['Volume'].rename('NVDA')
goog_volume = goog_data['Volume'].rename('GOOG')
aapl_volume = aapl_data['Volume'].rename('AAPL')
# Merge the closing prices and volume into a single DataFrame
stock_data = pd.concat([tsla_close, tsla_volume, nvda_close, nvda_volume, goog_close, goog_volume, aapl_close, aapl_volume], axis=1)
# Create a hierarchical index
stock_data.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples([
    ('TSLA', 'Close'),
    ('TSLA', 'Volume'),
    ('NVDA', 'Close'),
    ('NVDA', 'Volume'),
    ('GOOG', 'Close'),
    ('GOOG', 'Volume'),
    ('AAPL', 'Close'),
    ('AAPL', 'Volume'),   
])

# Display the first few rows of the DataFrame
print(stock_data.head())

# Create a DataFrame to store the daily price change status (Increase/Decrease)
price_daily_change_status = stock_data.xs('Close', axis=1, level=1).diff().applymap(lambda x: 'Increase' if x > 0 else 'Decrease')
price_daily_change_status['DayOfWeek'] = price_daily_change_status.index.day_name()

# Create a crosstab of the status data for each stock
crosstab_tsla = pd.crosstab(price_daily_change_status['DayOfWeek'], price_daily_change_status['TSLA'], rownames=['Day of Week'], colnames=['TSLA'])
crosstab_nvda = pd.crosstab(price_daily_change_status['DayOfWeek'], price_daily_change_status['NVDA'], rownames=['Day of Week'], colnames=['NVDA'])
crosstab_goog = pd.crosstab(price_daily_change_status['DayOfWeek'], price_daily_change_status['GOOG'], rownames=['Day of Week'], colnames=['GOOG'])
crosstab_aapl = pd.crosstab(price_daily_change_status['DayOfWeek'], price_daily_change_status['AAPL'], rownames=['Day of Week'], colnames=['AAPL'])
print(crosstab_tsla)
print(crosstab_nvda)
print(crosstab_goog)
print(crosstab_aapl)
# Plot the crosstab for each stock
crosstab_tsla.plot(kind='barh', stacked=True, title='TSLA Daily Performance by Day of the Week')
crosstab_nvda.plot(kind='barh', stacked=True, title='NVDA Daily Performance by Day of the Week')
crosstab_goog.plot(kind='barh', stacked=True, title='GOOG Daily Performance by Day of the Week')
crosstab_aapl.plot(kind='barh', stacked=True, title='AAPL Daily Performance by Day of the Week')

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Create the drawing canvas and subplots using the Object-oriented approach
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 4))
close_data = stock_data.xs('Close', axis=1, level=1)
volume_data = stock_data.xs('Volume', axis=1, level=1)
# Convert DateTimeIndex to a format compatible with NumPy
dates = close_data.index.to_numpy()

# Find the highest and lowest prices for TSLA
tsla_max_price = close_data['TSLA'].max()
tsla_min_price = close_data['TSLA'].min()
tsla_max_date = close_data['TSLA'].idxmax()
tsla_min_date = close_data['TSLA'].idxmin()

# Plot each stock's closing price
axes[0].plot(dates, close_data['TSLA'].values, color='blue', linewidth=2, marker='o', label='TSLA')
axes[0].plot(dates, close_data['NVDA'].values, linestyle='dashed', label='NVDA')
axes[0].plot(dates, close_data['GOOG'].values, linestyle = 'dashdot', label='GOOG')
axes[0].plot(dates, close_data['AAPL'].values, linestyle = 'dotted', label='AAPL')

# Set the title and labels
axes[0].set_title('Stock Closing Prices: TSLA, NVDA, GOOG, AAPL (April 2024 - June 2024)')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Date')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Close Price (USD)')
# Enable the legend
axes[0].legend(loc = "best")

# Annotate the highest price for TSLA
axes[0].annotate(f'Highest: {tsla_max_price:.2f}',
            xy=(tsla_max_date, tsla_max_price),
            xytext=(tsla_max_date, tsla_max_price + 20),
            arrowprops=dict(facecolor='green', shrink=0.05),
            fontsize=10, color='green', weight='bold')

# Annotate the lowest price for TSLA
axes[0].annotate(f'Lowest: {tsla_min_price:.2f}',
            xy=(tsla_min_date, tsla_min_price),
            xytext=(tsla_min_date, tsla_min_price - 20),
            arrowprops=dict(facecolor='red', shrink=0.05),
            fontsize=10, color='red', weight='bold')

# Plot each stock's volume
axes[1].plot(dates, volume_data['TSLA'].values, label='TSLA')
axes[1].plot(dates, volume_data['NVDA'].values, label='NVDA')
axes[1].plot(dates, volume_data['GOOG'].values, label='GOOG')
axes[1].plot(dates, volume_data['AAPL'].values, label='AAPL')
axes[1].legend(loc = "best")
props = {    
    'title': 'Stock Volumes: TSLA, NVDA, GOOG, AAPL (April 2024 - June 2024)',    
    'xlabel': 'Date',
    'ylabel': 'Volumes (1e8)',
    'yticks': [0, 2e8, 4e8, 6e8, 8e8],
    'yticklabels': ['zero', 'two', 'four', 'six', 'eight']}
axes[1].set(**props)

# Add grid lines for better readability
axes[0].grid(True)  
axes[1].grid(True) 
# Improve layout and show the plot
fig.autofmt_xdate()
plt.show()

from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter

# Calculate the average closing prices and total volume for each stock
average_close_prices = close_data.mean()
total_volume = volume_data.sum()
# Create a plotting canvas and the 1 * 2 grid for subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3))

# Define the x-axis positions
x0_positions = range(len(average_close_prices))
x1_positions = range(len(total_volume))

# Create the bar plot using ax.bar method
axes[0].bar(x0_positions, average_close_prices, color=['blue', 'orange', 'green', 'red'])
axes[1].bar(x1_positions, total_volume, color=['blue', 'orange', 'green', 'red'])

# Set the title and labels
axes[0].set_title('Average Closing Prices (April 2024 - June 2024)')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Stock')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Average Close Price (USD)')
axes[1].set_title('Total Volume (April 2024 - June 2024)')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Stock')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Total Volume (1e10)')

# Define a formatter function
def billions(x, pos):
    return '%1.1f' % (x * 1e-10)

# Apply the formatter to the y-axis to remove the 1e10 
axes[1].yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(billions))
# Set the x-axis tick labels to the stock names
axes[0].set_xticks(x0_positions)
axes[0].set_xticklabels(average_close_prices.index)
axes[1].set_xticks(x1_positions)
axes[1].set_xticklabels(total_volume.index)

# Display the plot
plt.show()

# Combine Pandas DataFrame plot method and matplotlib's subplots configuration for plotting panel

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(10, 8))

stock_data.plot(x=('TSLA', 'Close'), y=('GOOG', 'Close'), ax = axes[0, 1], title='TSLA vs GOOG Close Prices', kind = 'scatter', color='orange')
stock_data.plot(x=('TSLA', 'Close'), y=('AAPL', 'Close'), ax = axes[1, 0], title='TSLA vs AAPL Close Prices', kind = 'scatter', color='green')
stock_data.plot(x=('NVDA', 'Close'), y=('GOOG', 'Close'), ax = axes[1, 1], title='NVDA vs GOOG Close Prices', kind = 'scatter', color='red')
stock_data.plot(x=('NVDA', 'Close'), y=('AAPL', 'Close'), ax = axes[2, 0], title='NVDA vs AAPL Close Prices', kind = 'scatter', color='purple')

# Add grid lines for better readability
axes[0, 0].grid(True)  
axes[0, 1].grid(True) 
axes[0, 0].grid(True)  
axes[0, 1].grid(True) 
axes[2, 0].grid(True)  

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles and labels
plt.tight_layout()

# Display the plot
plt.show()

# Resample data to monthly frequency and calculate the mean
monthly_close_prices = close_data.resample('M').mean()

# Melt the data for easier plotting with Seaborn
monthly_close_prices_melted = monthly_close_prices.reset_index().melt(id_vars='Date', var_name='Stock', value_name='Close')
# Shorten the Date 
monthly_close_prices_melted['Date'] = monthly_close_prices_melted['Date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m')

# Create a factor plot (catplot) for average monthly closing prices
sns.set(style="whitegrid")
g = sns.catplot(
    x="Stock", 
    y="Close", 
    hue="Stock", 
    col="Date", 
    data=monthly_close_prices_melted, 
    kind="bar", 
    height=3.8,  
    aspect=0.8  
)

g.set_xticklabels(rotation=45)  # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
g.fig.suptitle('Average Monthly Closing Prices', y=1.02)
plt.show()
